Boston Marathon spectator guide: Tips for watching the race in person Updated: 10:38 AM EDT Apr 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ From the starting line in Hopkinton to the finish line in Boston's Copley Square, here's what you need to know to go watch the 130th Boston Marathon in person. 1 When do races begin?* 9:06 a.m. Wheelchair Men9:09 a.m. Wheelchair Women9:30 a.m. Handcycle and Duo Participants9:37 a.m. Professional Men9:47 a.m. Professional Women9:50 a.m. Para Athletics Divisions10 a.m. Wave 110:15 a.m. Wave 210:28 a.m. Wave 310:41 a.m. Wave 411:01 a.m. Wave 511:21 a.m. Wave 6 *Start times are subject to change 2 8 great places to watch Hopkinton: The starting line of the historic marathon is located on Main Street. Fans can watch the thrilling starts of 30,000 participants. Ashland: With some careful planning, a fan can watch their favorite participant running on Main Street, then hop on the Commuter Rail to see them again further down the course. Framingham: The train depot in the center of town is one of the most historic places to watch the race and its another convenient place to jump on the inbound Commuter Rail to meet your favorite runner in Boston.Natick: Crowds gather on both sides of the road near Fisk Pond and pack into Natick Common on Center Street.Wellesley: The "Scream Tunnel" at Wellesley College is just prior to the halfway point and is known as one of the loudest and most enthusiastic parts of the course. Newton: Runners are challenged by the hills but cheered onward toward Boston by crowds of fans on both sides of the road. Brookline: The course follows Beacon Street for nearly three miles, offering lots of room for spectators and plenty of nearby restaurants or shops. Boston: It's hard to beat the excitement of that final stretch on Boylston Street where athletes receive their medals and can celebrate with their families or fans at the meeting area located along Stuart Street between Berkeley and Clarendon Streets. Click here for a full map of the route! 3 How to track a runners' progress On race day, the B.A.A. will use a tracking tool that allows fans to search for participants based on name and/or bib number. Data about that runner's progress past official race checkpoints will be updated automatically.The tool is available through the B.A.A.'s Racing app, which is available through smartphone app stores. 4 Parking and road closures Parking is extremely limited in Boston's Back Bay neighborhood during race week, and garage access may be affected.The garage at 100 Clarendon, for example, is inaccessible during the marathon. Boston Common Garage also has limited access on the morning of the race.Other garages near the finish line include Prudential Center Parking and Copley Place Parking. Similar impacts are true throughout the length of the race course. 5 Using the MBTA to watch the marathon The MBTA announced service schedules to accommodate anticipated increased ridership during the Boston Marathon. The Green, Red, Orange, Blue and Silver lines will operate on a regular weekday schedule with additional service before and after the race. Buses will operate on a Saturday schedule with some planned detours around the track and other activities.All Commuter Rail lines will operate on a regular weekday schedule on Marathon Monday, with exceptions on the Framingham/Worcester Commuter Rail Line. The MBTA encourages riders to subscribe to T-Alerts for more information about bus route diversions and service interruptions. It happened Monday morning in the San Fernando Valley community of Pacoima, California. Video shows a low-flying plane strike a power line, triggering a small explosion, before plummeting about 30 feet to a parking lot below. According to officials with the Los Angeles Fire Department, a 70-year-old man was flying the Cessna 172.After striking the power line, the plane nosedived into an O'Reilly’s auto shop parking lot below.Local news outlets report that the plane was returning to the nearby Whiteman Airport at the time of the crash. The pilot, who was the only person in the plane, was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment. His condition is unknown.No additional injuries were reported.Officials with the Federal Aviation Administration say the crash is under investigation. LOS ANGELES —Dramatic video shows the moment a small plane clipped a power line before falling from the sky in Southern California. It happened Monday morning in the San Fernando Valley community of Pacoima, California. Video shows a low-flying plane strike a power line, triggering a small explosion, before plummeting about 30 feet to a parking lot below. According to officials with the Los Angeles Fire Department, a 70-year-old man was flying the Cessna 172.After striking the power line, the plane nosedived into an O'Reilly’s auto shop parking lot below.Local news outlets report that the plane was returning to the nearby Whiteman Airport at the time of the crash. The pilot, who was the only person in the plane, was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment. His condition is unknown. No additional injuries were reported.Officials with the Federal Aviation Administration say the crash is under investigation. Piscatella has spent more than 90 years serving the Catholic Church, joining the Dominican order when she was 17. Above video: Study confirms being grateful may help you live longerThe Long Island native has been a member of the Sisters of St. Dominic of Amityville since 1931. Through her decades of service, Piscatella served as a teacher, taking on various subjects in Catholic schools across the area until she retired at 84. In fact, teaching is the secret to longevity, according to Piscatella."Teach until you die," she told the New York Post in 2025, when asked about her secret to a long and healthy life.“You have to be a saint before you get to heaven,” she said.Piscatella has seen 10 different popes in her lifetime. And in celebration of her 113th birthday, Pope Leo XIV issued a proclamation celebrating her milestone birthday, according to WABC-TV in New York.Piscatella has held the title of the world's oldest living nun for a little over a year now, according to Guinness World Records.She became the oldest nun after the death of Brazil's Sister Inah Canabarro Lucas on April 30, 2025.
